news_drafts.headline: North Lanarkshire's Routes to Work engaged 127 out-of-work parents in Q1 2026/27 against a target of 180
news_drafts.lead:
Routes to Work Ltd, the employability programme reported to North Lanarkshire's Enterprise and Fair Work Committee, engaged 127 out-of-work parents in the first quarter of 2026/27 against a target of 180. The monitoring report also shows 18 in-work parents engaged against a target of 31. Both measures are marked red.

The paper says "in Q1 for 2026/27 there is a shortfall in the engagement of parents". It states that job outcomes for parents have still been met.

The report says the issue was identified in July 2026 and that steps were put in place after it was identified. The paper, as verified by our desk, does not set out in the material available what those steps are or when engagement is expected to reach target.
news_drafts.paper_title: Routes to Work Ltd – Performance & Financial Monitoring Report

news_drafts.headline: North Lanarkshire adult social care forecast to overspend by £5.759m on £191.677m budget for 2026/27
news_drafts.lead:
North Lanarkshire's adult social care service is forecast to overspend by £5.759m, or 3.0%, on a budget of £191.677m for 2026/27. The figure is in the budget monitoring report to the Adult Care and Social Work Committee, covering 1 April to 11 September 2026. It sits in payments to other bodies and transfer payments.

The report says the overspend is primarily in Care at Home and Independent Care Homes. It describes the projections as demand led and based on full-year costs for current and anticipated clients, so they will change through the year.

The report says any overspend for the year ending 31 March 2027 will be fully funded by the Integration Joint Board's reserves. It anticipates a year-end drawdown of £1.647m and gives total planned reserve use for 2026/27 as £5.008m.

A separate performance report shows the projected outturn for North Lanarkshire Council at quarter 1 of 2026/27 as a £2.627m overspend, against a target of zero or better. The same dashboard shows an overspend of £5.939m at quarter 1 of 2025/26 and an underspend, shown as £0.445, at quarter 4. The report's narrative does not explain the movement.
news_drafts.paper_title: Revenue and Capital Budget Monitoring Report: Adult Social Care Period 6: 1 April to 11 September 2026

news_drafts.headline: North Lanarkshire's housing revenue account gap for 2027/28 falls to £4.253m from £7.484m
news_drafts.lead:
North Lanarkshire Council's housing revenue account, the separate ring-fenced account for its own housing stock, paid for by rents, now has a budget gap of £4.253m for 2027/28. The medium-term financial plan presented in August 2026 put the gap at £7.484m. Revised planning assumptions reduced it by £3.231m, according to the paper going to the Housing Committee on 4 November 2026.

The paper sets cost pressures of £7.581m against base budget reductions of £3.328m, which leaves the £4.253m gap. It says the gap is to be reviewed at the December 2026 Council meeting, when estimates and rent levels for 2027/28 are to be approved.

Appendix 2 gives revised gaps for later years. For 2028/29 the gap is £9.751m, against £9.813m in the medium-term plan. For 2029/30 it is £13.998m, against £12.590m. The paper says unbudgeted pressures will be managed where possible through in-year action or unallocated reserves, with recurring impacts addressed in future medium-term financial plans.

findings.paper_title: Revenue Monitoring Report Council Summary - 1 April to 11 September 2026
findings.headline: The HRA projects breakeven, with a £1.176m employee cost underspend offset by £0.438m of administration overspends and a £0.578m income under-recovery from reduced capital recharges.
findings.detail: The paper links the employee cost underspend to vacancies in the HRA capital programme and to ongoing recruitment challenges. Agency staff are being used to cover these vacancies, and the reduced capital recharges are also linked to those vacancies.
findings.matters: A housing account that balances only through vacancy underspends, with agency cover and lost capital recharges, shows a recruitment pressure that other councils' HRA capital programmes may share.
findings.figures: £1.176m employee cost underspend; £0.438m administration overspend; £0.578m income under-recovery
findings.quote: An underspend of £1.176m is projected within Employee Costs

findings.paper_title: Revenue Monitoring Report Council Summary - 1 April to 11 September 2026
findings.headline: Education and Families projects an underspend of £0.779m, mainly from employee costs (£0.631m) and payments to other bodies (£0.840m) linked to ASN and family placements.
findings.detail: The paper attributes the underspend to vacancies and staffing structures, and to lower than anticipated costs for ASN and family placements. These are partly offset by overspends in administration costs and supplies and services, and an income under-recovery of £0.274m.
findings.matters: A service moving from a placement-driven pressure to an underspend is a change other councils with ASN and placement costs will want to compare.
findings.figures: £0.779m underspend; £0.631m employee costs; £0.840m payments to other bodies; £0.274m income under-recovery
findings.quote: Education and Families are reporting a projected underspend of £0.779m.

findings.paper_title: Revenue Monitoring Report Council Summary - 1 April to 11 September 2026
findings.headline: Council adult health and social care provision to the IJB is projecting an overspend of £1.647m, with £5.759m of overspends in payments to other bodies and transfer payments linked to increased demand.
findings.detail: The paper attributes the overspend mainly to demand in Care at Home and Independent Care homes and to winter planning spend, partly offset by an employee cost underspend of £3.225m from slippage in recruitment and £1.165m of over-recovered income.
findings.matters: A council's contribution to an IJB overspend of this kind is a demand-led pressure that other councils with integrated health and social care budgets will recognise.
findings.figures: £1,647,194 projected overspend; £5.759m payments and transfers; £3.225m employee cost underspend; £1.165m over-recovered income
findings.quote: transfer payments of £5.759m linked to increased demand

findings.paper_title: Revenue Monitoring Report Council Summary - 1 April to 11 September 2026
findings.headline: The Change Management Fund is forecast at £6.691m after one-off savings costs of £1.508m and known commitments of £2.059m, from £10.258m at 2025/26 year end.
findings.detail: Appendix 4 shows the revised one-off costs of approved savings drawn from the Change Management Fund, and further known commitments. The forecast balance to support future budget challenges is then £6.691m.
findings.matters: Drawdown of a one-off fund that is used to fund savings delivery is a pattern other councils can track against their own transformation reserves.
findings.figures: £10,258k opening balance; £1,508k revised one-off savings costs; £2,059k known commitments; £6,691k forecast balance
findings.quote: Revised one-off costs of approved savings (2,059)

findings.paper_title: Revenue Monitoring Report Council Summary - 1 April to 11 September 2026
findings.headline: Funds set aside for future budget pressures are projected at £20.761m at 31 March 2027, including the £1.334m projected surplus.
findings.detail: The paper states that funds set aside for future budget pressures, which stood at £19.427m, rise to £20.761m once the projected surplus is included. These balances support future budget challenges under the approved reserves policy.
findings.matters: A projected rise in unallocated reserves in the first half of the year is a position a finance director can compare with their own reserve trajectory.
findings.figures: £20.761m projected at year end; £19.427m opening; £1.334m surplus
findings.quote: the General Fund will include funds set aside for future budget pressures of £20.761m
